children: UGI plans to spin off its global liquefied petroleum gas business into two public companies.

The distributor of energy products on Wednesday said the spinoff, approved by its board, is part of the company's transformation strategy and should position both companies for long-term growth. The separation is expected to be completed during the second half of 2027.

After the spinoff's completion, the new UGI will be a natural gas infrastructure company for customers in the mid-atlantic regions. The new liquefied petroleum gas company is expected to be a distributor in Europe, while also being a retail propane distributor in the U.S.

Under the proposed spinoff plan, UGI shareholders will retain their current shares and receive a pro-rata distribution of shares of the new LPG company's stock. After the spinoff, the new UGI may retain a stake of up to 20% in the new LPG company.
The spinoff came as UGI on Wednesday posted a fourth-quarter profit of $8 million, or 4 cents a share, compared with a loss of $13 million, or 6 cents a share, the year earlier.
Revenue fell to $1.16 billion from $1.2 billion the year before.
